liberal-majority-in-canadian-parliament-.question: Liberal majority in Canadian Parliament by June 30?
liberal-majority-in-canadian-parliament-.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Liberal Party of Canada holds a majority of seats in the House of Commons for any period of time between December 12, 2025 and June 30, 2026, otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "No" if Parliament is dissolved before June 30, 2026. 

This markets resolution will be based solely on the number of seats held by the Liberal Party of Canada, not any alliance or coalition of which it may be a part.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the Canadian government or a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Prime Minister Mark Carney's Liberal Party, holding 169 seats in the 343-seat House of Commons following the April 2025 federal election minority government victory, stands on the brink of a majority requiring 172 seats, fueling trader consensus at near-certainty for Yes. Recent floor-crossings by opposition MPs, including NDP's Lori Idlout last month, combined with double-digit national polling leads, have positioned Liberals as heavy favorites in today's three critical federal byelections in ridings vacated by recent departures. Projections from 338Canada and others anticipate Liberal wins in all three, potentially securing majority immediately. While exceeding 90% implied probability, rare scenarios like unexpected byelection upsets, reverse defections, or legal challenges to results could delay or derail this outcome before June 30 resolution.

will-parti-qubcois-win-the-most-seats-in.question: Will Parti Québécois win the most seats in the 2026 Quebec general election?
will-parti-qubcois-win-the-most-seats-in.description:
Parliamentary elections to elect all 125 seats of the National Assembly of Quebec are scheduled to take place in Quebec on October 5, 2026.

This market will resolve to the political party that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Quebec as a result of this election.

If voting in the 2026 Quebec general election does not occur by January 31, 2027, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie for the most seats won between this party and any other, this market will resolve in favor of the party that won the most valid votes in the respective election. If this also results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose listed abbreviation comes first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by Élections Québec (https://www.electionsquebec.qc.ca).

eventMetadata.context_description: Parti Québécois leads trader consensus at 57.5% implied probability to secure the most seats in Quebec's National Assembly in the October 5, 2026 general election, reflecting poll aggregators like 338Canada projecting PQ with 63 seats versus PLQ's 47 despite the Liberals' slight popular vote edge around 36% to PQ's 29%. This positioning stems from PQ's efficient vote distribution in francophone ridings outside Montreal, bolstered by four by-election victories since late 2025 and sustained momentum after Premier François Legault's January resignation amid 25% approval ratings. PLQ at 34% benefits from new leader Charles Milliard's February bump narrowing the gap in March Léger polls, but recent surveys show PQ regaining ground. CAQ languishes at 7.5% following Christine Fréchette's April 12 leadership win, facing steep recovery challenges in a first-past-the-post system six months out.

will-the-democratic-party-control-the-ho.question: Will the Democratic Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
will-the-democratic-party-control-the-ho.description:
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus heavily favors Democrats reclaiming House control in the November 2026 midterms, driven by the historical midterm penalty for the president's party—Republicans defend a razor-thin majority after narrow 2024 gains under President Trump. Recent generic ballot polls reinforce this positioning, with Emerson's January survey showing Democrats ahead 48%-42%, Marist's national edge at 53%-44%, and YouGov noting a narrowing but persistent lead through March. Vulnerable GOP seats in battleground districts and a competitive electoral map amplify Democratic opportunities, while April special elections in Georgia and elsewhere provide early momentum tests. Trump's improving approval offers Republicans some counterbalance ahead of primaries, though rapid shifts remain possible.

Determination of which party controls the Senate after the 2026 US Senate elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

Recent GOP anxieties have intensified following March polling in Texas showing Democrat James Talarico leading Sen. Vulnerabilities in battlegrounds like North Carolina's open seat, Maine's Susan Collins, and potential plays in Alaska and Ohio counterbalance Republican defenses in red states and pickups eyed in Michigan and Georgia, with fundraising edges aiding Democrats ahead of spring primaries.
